audit_findings.title: The 2025 anchor may contain a nonrepeatable tax-reserve benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $141 million tax benefit, equal to 34.1% of the $413.9 million anchor; if fully removed, computed base value falls about $14.85 per share to $34.22
audit_findings.mechanism: The benefit enters reported net income and therefore the 2025 OE anchor, which is capitalized throughout the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 provision for income taxes includes decreases related to changes in unrecognized tax benefits and tax credits, offset by an increase related to foreign tax effects due to the Company's mix of earnings.
audit_findings.explanation: The $141 million benefit is demonstrated by the filed tax reconciliation, but its precise inclusion in OE and overlap with the separately identified $33 million tax item remain unresolved. Because full retention would materially inflate every scenario, this is capable of changing the intrinsic-value and buy-below conclusions.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $141 million through reported net income into OE, identify overlap with the $33 million separately judged tax item, determine sustainable cash taxes, and rerun all scenarios using the double-count-free normalized anchor.

audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include factoring-funded operating liquidity
audit_findings.magnitude: $406 million of receivables would have been outstanding without factoring at 2026-06-30, equal to 58.8% of the $691 million cash add-back and $3.22 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Factoring can convert required operating receivables into cash; treating that cash as surplus in the bridge while retaining the working-capital benefit in OE can count the same liquidity twice.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on the original terms of receivables sold for certain programs and actual outstanding balance of receivables under servicing agreements, the Company estimates that $346 million and $385 million of these receivables would have been outstanding as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively, had they not been sold under these factoring programs.
audit_findings.explanation: Routine factoring and the $406 million receivable displacement are demonstrated, but the record does not establish that any specific portion of the $691 million cash balance is factoring proceeds or required operating liquidity. Excluding $406 million solely from the bridge would reduce base value to about $45.85 per share, but an OE working-capital correction could add further impact that is presently unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a June 2026 pro forma balance sheet and cash-flow history without factoring, establish the minimum operating-cash requirement, and rerun the bridge and working-capital component of OE without double counting.

audit_findings.title: Already-accrued uncertain tax claims may be absent from both future OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $183 million of unrecognized tax benefits plus $26 million of accrued interest at 2025-12-31, or $209 million total; latest unrecognized tax benefits were $185 million at 2026-06-30; $209 million equals $1.66 per share and 3.4% of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash settlement of an already-accrued tax liability can bypass future earnings-based OE, requiring either explicit future cash outflows or a bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Due to uncertainties in the timing of the effective settlement of tax positions with taxing authorities, management is unable to determine the timing of payments related to uncertain tax liabilities and these amounts are included in the "2031 and beyond" line item.
audit_findings.explanation: The accrued claims are demonstrated, while their omission from OE is plausible rather than traced. Even deducting the full filed year-end tax-benefit and interest balances reduces base value only from $49.07 to about $47.41 per share and does not alter the valuation range relative to the $71.19 market price. Any unaccrued adverse tax outcome is a separate, unquantified risk.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile current and long-term tax liabilities, unrecognized benefits, accrued interest, expected settlements, and OE tax adjustments; confirm that the $209 million claim is captured exactly once.

audit_findings.title: Environmental reserves represent future cash claims not necessarily captured by earnings-based OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $287 million to $524 million of estimated remediation expenditures at 2026-06-30, equal to $2.27 to $4.15 per share and 4.6% to 8.5% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Payments against previously accrued remediation reserves consume cash without a corresponding future expense, so they must enter projected OE as cash outflows or be deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Estimated future environmental expenditures for undiscounted remediation costs ranged from $285 million to $509 million with a best estimate or minimum of $285 million at December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The existing remediation claim is demonstrated, and the valuation bridge contains no environmental deduction. The precise adjustment remains unresolved because recurring environmental expenses and capital expenditures already retained in OE must not be counted again. The filed range is large enough to materially change intrinsic value and the buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Build a site-level payment schedule separating reserve settlements from recurring environmental operating costs and capital expenditures, then rerun the valuation using either explicit OE cash payments or one present-value bridge deduction.

audit_findings.title: Retirement-plan funding can exceed the expense retained in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed $174 million net funded deficit at 2025-12-31, or $1.38 per share; contributions exceeded expense by $60 million in 2025 and $48 million in first-half 2026; sustainable excess funding is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash contributions exceeding pension and postretirement expense reduce owner cash flow; alternatively, an existing unfunded claim can be recognized in the bridge. The 2025 plan amendment also produces future accounting credits without equivalent cash inflow.
audit_findings.evidence: While changes in obligations do not correspond directly to cash funding requirements, it is an indication of the amount the Company will be required to contribute to the plans in future years.
audit_findings.explanation: The deficit and recent cash-versus-expense differences are demonstrated, but the record does not establish a sustainable annual funding shortfall. Treating only the $174 million net deficit as a bridge claim would reduce base value by about 2.8%, while capitalization of a persistent contribution gap could be substantially larger. The amendment's $208 million obligation reduction and related prior-service credits further prevent a reliable materiality conclusion without a plan-level reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Obtain plan-level funded status, legally usable surpluses, expected employer contributions, benefit-payment funding sources, and the amendment's expense effects; rerun OE or the bridge with a single double-count-free treatment.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated cash may not belong entirely to Eastman common shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: $79 million reported noncontrolling interest at 2026-06-30; even deducting the entire amount would reduce value by only $0.63 per share, or 1.3% of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding all consolidated cash to equity attributable to Eastman while excluding minority earnings from OE can overstate the bridge unless minority-owned cash or the corresponding NCI claim is removed.
audit_findings.evidence: The consolidated financial statements include assets, liabilities, sales revenue, and expenses of all majority-owned subsidiaries and joint ventures in which a controlling interest is maintained.
audit_findings.explanation: Cash ownership by entity is unresolved, but the entire filed NCI claim provides a conservative scale comparison. A full $79 million deduction would lower base value only to about $48.44 per share and would not alter the valuation conclusion relative to the $71.19 price; the minority share of cash alone should be no larger than this claim absent contrary evidence.
audit_findings.action: Identify cash and short-term investments held by each less-than-100%-owned consolidated entity and either exclude the minority-owned portion from cash or deduct the corresponding NCI claim.
